daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo on Monday inaugurated Suahasil Nazara as Finance Minister, replacing Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa in a sudden reshuffle. The new minister said he was telephoned Monday morning and had not yet communicated with his predecessor. Analysts cited multiple factors behind the change, including market confidence issues and conflicts with regional governments, while reports suggested Purbaya objected to Danantara's Rp 120 trillion state dividend requirement.

  • The Anti-Corruption Commission (KPK) arrested a Director General at ATR/BPN Ministry and 16 others in an operation related to land rights processing in Bogor, seizing hundreds of billions of rupiah in 20 suitcases; those detained include Fahd Arafiq and a former Kebumen regent.
  • PDIP leader Megawati expelled Achmad Hidayat from the party after he visited former president Jokowi.
  • The Home Affairs Minister made women's empowerment and child protection mandatory programs for regional governments, after the government signed a joint decree on the matter.
  • DPR Commission XI leadership expressed confidence that President Prabowo carefully considered the Finance Minister replacement.
  • An individual challenged the traffic law at the Constitutional Court, requesting that expired driving licenses remain renewable.
  • The DPD and KMOU discussed human resources for the blue economy.
  • Hanura party cadres in Yogyakarta were called to serve as the vanguard at the grassroots level.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia is turning its BRICS membership into global influence, with President Prabowo's attendance at the summit said to serve national interests. Indonesia is seeking to establish critical mineral supply chains with Latin America and exploring a preferential trade agreement with Mercosur as a pathway toward comprehensive economic partnership.

  • The Indonesian Navy is preparing to escort the Garibaldi as it arrives in Indonesian waters, with a naval parade involving 102 warships scheduled in Jakarta Bay featuring the carrier's first appearance.
  • Germany opened the possibility of procuring additional Airbus A400M transport aircraft for Indonesia, while also seeking broader economic ties amid global shifts.
  • Indonesia and Bulgaria are seeking to boost trade and investment.
  • Pertamina is exploring upstream oil investments in Guyana and Suriname.
  • Indonesia and New Zealand are expanding a renewable energy program in Maluku.

Other

Financial markets reacted calmly to Nazara's appointment as Finance Minister, with economists expecting him to strengthen Indonesia's fiscal position and address fiscal policy challenges. State holding company Danantara is ready to discuss dividend payments with the new minister. The new Finance Minister is expected to fix problems at customs and tax agencies.

  • The National Transportation Safety Committee (KNKT) responded to narratives about KM Virgo Transport 8's circling route before it sank, with Basarnas deploying KRI Canopus to join the search for victims; the wreckage is located at a shallow depth of 30 meters.
  • Indonesia may require global digital platforms to open local offices.
  • The government refined the Giant Sea Wall master plan to curb Java coastal flooding.
  • The government built a bioethanol center in Lampung with production capacity of 60 kiloliters per year to bolster energy security.
  • Four East Kalimantan companies were sealed amid fire investigation, with three firms receiving sanctions including warnings and permit suspensions.
